system: SAMPLE, replace every value: a notes app with a summarise button
notes: A filled-in sample to copy and overwrite. Every verification here is not_run with no date, so every threat is open. Nothing in this file was tested against anything. Set as_of to the day the model was last made true.
assumptions: The server is reachable from the internet over HTTPS only.
The model provider is a separate company reached over its public API.
out_of_scope: The hosting provider's own platform and staff.

assets.name: notes
assets.why: Private text written by each user; a leak or a silent edit cannot be undone.

assets.name: session tokens
assets.why: Whoever holds one can act as that user until it expires.

assets.name: model API key
assets.why: It spends money on the owner's account and reaches every prompt sent with it.

assets.name: request log
assets.why: Shows who did what and when; it must not also hold note text or keys.

actors.name: author of a web page that a user pastes into a note

zones.name: Browser
zones.trust: Controlled by the person using it. Nothing it sends is trusted until the server has checked it.

zones.name: Server
zones.trust: Controlled by the operator. The only place rules are enforced.

zones.name: Model provider
zones.trust: A third party. What it returns is input to validate, not an instruction.

threats.scenario: A signed-in user changes the note id in a request and reads or overwrites another user's notes, because the server checks that someone is signed in but not that the note is theirs.
threats.impact: Any user's private notes are readable and editable by any other user.
threats.likelihood: likely if the check is missing: it needs only a changed number in a request

threats.scenario: The author of a web page that a user pastes into a note hides an instruction in the text, the model follows it, and its reply asks the server to delete or rewrite notes.
threats.impact: Notes are changed or removed without the user asking for it.

threats.scenario: An anonymous visitor finds the summarise route and calls it in a loop, so the model API key is charged until the account limit is reached and the feature stops for everyone.
threats.impact: A bill nobody planned for, and the summarise button fails for every user.

threats.scenario: The server logs each outbound request with its headers, so the model API key and note text sit in the request log file where an operator or a backup reader can copy them.
threats.impact: The key is exposed to everyone who can read logs or backups.
threats.likelihood: likely if request logging was added without a redaction list

threats.scenario: An operator with database access reads users' notes, because they are stored as plain text.
threats.impact: Private notes are visible to whoever administers the database.
threats.likelihood_why: One operator, who is also the owner.

threats.scenario: An anonymous visitor guesses passwords at the sign-in route without limit and obtains a session token for a real account.
threats.impact: Full access to that user's notes.

mitigations.what: Every note query filters by the signed-in user's id, taken from the session and never from the request.
mitigations.where: REPLACE: file and function, for example notes.py get_note()

mitigations.what: The model's reply is parsed, checked against a schema and mapped to a fixed list of actions; it can only return summary text, and no reply can trigger a write.
The summarise route requires a session and allows a fixed number of calls per user per hour, with a daily ceiling for the whole account.
mitigations.where: REPLACE: file and function, and the config key holding the limits

mitigations.what: The logger writes method, path, status and request id only; headers and bodies are never logged.

verifications.how: Test: user B requests user A's note id and gets 404; user A requests the same id and gets 200.
Test: replies that are not JSON, lack a field, carry an unknown key or name an action outside the list are each refused and no note changes.
Test: the call at the limit succeeds, the next is refused with 429 and a Retry-After header, and no model request is sent for it.
Test: send a request carrying a marker string in a header and in the body, then search the log file for the marker; it must not appear.
